Access-Control-Allow-Headers.description: Specifies which HTTP headers can be used during a cross-origin request, returned in preflight responses.

schema.example: Authorization, Origin, X-Requested-With, Content-Type, Accept, Access-Control-Request-Method

Access-Control-Allow-Methods.description: Indicates which HTTP methods are permitted for cross-origin requests, typically returned in preflight responses.

schema.example: GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: Specifies which origin(s) may access the resource.

Access-Control-Expose-Headers.description: Lists the response headers that browsers are allowed to access from JavaScript beyond the default restricted set.

Allow.description: Lists the HTTP methods supported by the endpoint; returned alongside a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.

schema.example: GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK

Cache-Control.description: Directives controlling caching behavior for the response.

Content-Disposition.description: Provides the original filename, as well as additional file attributes. Non-ASCII filenames can be encoded using UTF-8, but require special escape sequences - see spec/docs for details.

Content-Range.description: Byte range actually returned, plus the total size of the file: `bytes [start]-[end]/[total]`, e.g. `bytes 0-99/138937`. Only present on a `206 Partial Content` response.

ETag.description: Entity tag used for caching and optimistic concurrency control.

ETag-optional.description:
Entity tag used for caching and optimistic concurrency control.

**Note**: ETag is not included for collections which are too big.

Expires.description: Point in time after which the unfinished resumable upload is discarded, if it is not completed before then.

Location-created.description: URL of the newly created resource.

Repr-Digest.description: Cryptographic digest of the file's full content, in RFC 9530 structured-field format. Only `sha-256` is supported: `sha-256=:[base64]:`, where the base64 payload is the raw 32-byte SHA-256 digest. Omitted if the element has no stored hash yet (e.g. records predating this feature).

Upload-Complete.description: Structured boolean indicating whether the upload is finished: `?1` for complete, `?0` for still in progress.

Upload-Length.description: Total number of bytes the finished file will have. Optional - omitted when the total size is not known ahead of time.

Upload-Limit.description: Structured field listing the server's limits for this upload: `max-age` (seconds an unfinished upload is kept alive since its first request), `max-size` (maximum total file size in bytes), `min-append-size` (minimum size in bytes for a non-final chunk) and `max-append-size` (maximum size in bytes per chunk).

Upload-Offset.description: Number of bytes already stored for the resumable upload. On a request, it must match the upload's current offset exactly; on a response, it reflects the offset after the request was processed.

If-Match.name: If-Match
If-Match.description: Used primarily for optimistic concurrency control — the request is only executed if the resource's `ETag` matches the provided value.

If-None-Match.name: If-None-Match
If-None-Match.description: Used primarily for caching — skips re-downloading an unchanged resource by returning `304 Not Modified` if the resource's `ETag` matches the provided value.

data.name: Yellow
data.content: Yellow is the color between green and orange on the spectrum of light. It is evoked by light with a dominant wavelength of roughly 575–585 nm. It is a primary color in subtractive color systems, used in painting or color printing. In the RGB color model, used to create colors on television and computer screens, yellow is a secondary color made by combining red and green at equal intensity. Carotenoids give the characteristic yellow color to autumn leaves, corn, canaries, daffodils, and lemons, as well as egg yolks, buttercups, and bananas. They absorb light energy and protect plants from photo damage in some cases. Sunlight has a slight yellowish hue when the Sun is near the horizon, due to atmospheric scattering of shorter wavelengths (green, blue, and violet).

data.name: Additive color model
data.content: Additive color or additive mixing is a property of a color model that predicts the appearance of colors made by coincident component lights, i.e. the perceived color can be predicted by summing the numeric representations of the component colors. Modern formulations of Grassmann's laws describe the additivity in the color perception of light mixtures in terms of algebraic equations. Additive color predicts perception and not any sort of change in the photons of light themselves. These predictions are only applicable in the limited scope of color matching experiments where viewers match small patches of uniform color isolated against a grey or black background.

200.description: File found and returned as a stream. No `Range` header was sent, so the complete file is returned.

206.description: Partial file content returned, matching the requested `Range`. The end of an open-ended or overlong range is clamped to the file's actual length rather than rejected.

get.description: Retrieves the binary file attached to a specific element. Supports partial downloads via the `Range` header.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Requests a single byte range of the file instead of the full content: `bytes=[start]-[end]`, `bytes=[start]-` (open-ended) or `bytes=-[suffixLength]` (last N bytes) - e.g. `bytes=0-1048575` for the first megabyte. Multiple comma-separated ranges are not supported and fail with `400 Bad Request`.

201.description: The complete file was uploaded directly (`Upload-Complete: ?1`, or the header was omitted) and is now attached to the element. Returned without a response body.

204.description: A resumable upload (`Upload-Complete: ?0`) was created successfully. Its URL is returned in the `Location` header - continue it with `PATCH`, inspect it with `HEAD`, or abort it with `DELETE` against that URL.

400.description: General issues with the request, e.g. a malformed or inconsistent upload header, or an uploaded chunk that violates the configured min/max chunk size.

post.description: Creates a new file for an element, either by uploading the complete file directly or by starting a resumable upload. Fails if the element already has a file attached.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: Id of the element the file is attached to.

parameters.name: Upload-Complete
parameters.description: `?1` uploads the request body as the complete, final file. `?0` starts a resumable upload instead - the request body, if any, is stored as the first chunk. Omitting the header behaves like `?1`.

parameters.name: Upload-Length
parameters.description: Total size in bytes of the finished file. Only read when starting a resumable upload (`Upload-Complete: ?0`); optional even then.

parameters.name: Content-Disposition
parameters.description: Original filename of the uploaded file, used to derive the file's extension. Falls back to `bin` if omitted or if no extension can be parsed.

parameters.name: Repr-Digest
parameters.description: Cryptographic digest of the complete file, checked against the uploaded content once the direct upload finishes. Only `sha-256` is supported. A mismatch fails with `400 Bad Request` and the file is not stored. `Content-Digest` is accepted as a fallback if `Repr-Digest` is absent. Only meaningful for a complete (non-resumable) upload; for a resumable upload, verify the digest on the completing `PATCH` request instead.

201.description: The complete file was uploaded directly (`Upload-Complete: ?1`, or the header was omitted) and is now attached to the element, replacing any previous file. Returned without a response body.

204.description: A resumable upload (`Upload-Complete: ?0`) was created successfully. Its URL is returned in the `Location` header - continue it with `PATCH`, inspect it with `HEAD`, or abort it with `DELETE` against that URL.

400.description: General issues with the request, e.g. a malformed or inconsistent upload header, or an uploaded chunk that violates the configured min/max chunk size.

put.description: Creates or replaces the file of an element, either by uploading the complete file directly or by starting a resumable upload. Unlike `POST`, this succeeds even if the element already has a file attached - the existing file is replaced.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: Id of the element whose file is to be created or replaced.

parameters.name: Upload-Complete
parameters.description: `?1` uploads the request body as the complete, final file. `?0` starts a resumable upload instead - the request body, if any, is stored as the first chunk. Omitting the header behaves like `?1`.

parameters.name: Upload-Length
parameters.description: Total size in bytes of the finished file. Only read when starting a resumable upload (`Upload-Complete: ?0`); optional even then.

parameters.name: Content-Disposition
parameters.description: Original filename of the uploaded file, used to derive the file's extension. Falls back to `bin` if omitted or if no extension can be parsed.

parameters.name: Repr-Digest
parameters.description: Cryptographic digest of the complete file, checked against the uploaded content once the direct upload finishes. Only `sha-256` is supported. A mismatch fails with `400 Bad Request` and the existing file (if any) is left untouched. `Content-Digest` is accepted as a fallback if `Repr-Digest` is absent. Only meaningful for a complete (non-resumable) upload; for a resumable upload, verify the digest on the completing `PATCH` request instead.

401.description: The provided token is either invalid or expired.

404.description: No resumable upload with this id exists, it already expired or completed, or it belongs to a different user.

409.description: Another request is currently modifying the upload (per-upload lock); retry after a short pause.

delete.description: Aborts a resumable upload: already-uploaded chunks are removed from storage and the upload itself ceases to exist. The target element is left untouched. Only the user who created the upload can delete it.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: Id of the resumable upload, as returned in the `Location` header of the request that created it.

204.description: Resumable upload found. Its current state is returned entirely through response headers - there is no response body.

401.description: The provided token is either invalid or expired.

404.description: No resumable upload with this id exists, it already expired or completed, or it belongs to a different user.

head.description: Retrieves the current state of a resumable upload without transferring any of its already-uploaded data. Only the user who created the upload can query it.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: Id of the resumable upload, as returned in the `Location` header of the request that created it.

204.description:
The chunk was stored successfully.  
Specific meaning depends on `Upload-Complete`:

- `?0`: The chunk was appended, and the upload remains open for further chunks. Its new state is returned in the response headers.
- `?1`: The chunk was appended and the upload is now complete - the uploaded chunks were merged and attached as the target element's file, and the resumable upload no longer exists.

400.description: General issues with the request, e.g. a missing or malformed `Upload-Offset` header, a `Content-Type` other than `application/partial-upload`, or an uploaded chunk that violates the configured min/max chunk size.

401.description: The provided token is either invalid or expired.

404.description: No resumable upload with this id exists, it already completed, it belongs to a different user, or the current user has since lost `UPDATE` access to the upload's target element.

409.description: The `Upload-Offset` in the request does not match the upload's current offset, or the appended chunk would exceed the upload's declared `Upload-Length`. Also returned while another request is currently modifying the upload (per-upload lock).

410.description: The upload has expired and its data has already been discarded.

patch.description: Appends the next chunk to a resumable upload. Set `Upload-Complete: ?1` on the chunk that finishes the upload - the request body may be empty, which completes an upload without transmitting further data. A non-final chunk smaller than the minimum chunk size is rejected, except a body of exactly zero bytes, which is accepted as a no-op status check. Every body is capped at `file.uploadMaxChunkSizeInBytes`.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: Id of the resumable upload, as returned in the `Location` header of the request that created it.

parameters.name: Upload-Offset
parameters.description: Byte offset the appended chunk starts at. Must match the upload's current `Upload-Offset` exactly, otherwise the request fails with `409 Conflict`.

parameters.name: Upload-Complete
parameters.description: **Required** on `PATCH` (`400 Bad Request` if missing). `?1` marks this as the final chunk, completing the upload; `?0` keeps the upload open for further chunks.

parameters.name: Repr-Digest
parameters.description: Cryptographic digest of the complete (reassembled) file. Only read on the chunk that sets `Upload-Complete: ?1`, and checked against the merged file once assembled. Only `sha-256` is supported. A mismatch fails with `400 Bad Request`; the upload's target element keeps its previous file, if any (TODO: the upload is currently deleted on a failed completion - undecided). `Content-Digest` is accepted as a fallback if `Repr-Digest` is absent.
